column1: # What the upstream-drift workflow watches, and the single source of truth for it.
# build/check-upstream.sh reads this; it knows how to query each ecosystem but nothing about which
# components this repository binds. Adding a native SDK means adding a row here.
# Columns are single-tab-separated.
#   group    reporting group - one GitHub issue per group, titled with this text
#   label    how the component is named inside the issue
#   kind     cocoapods | maven | github-release | github-tag
#   pin      the MSBuild property in Directory.Build.props holding the pinned version
#   locator  kind-specific: pod name, groupId:artifactId[:packaging][@repo], or owner/repo
#   confirm  download URL template with {version}, or "-" to derive it from the locator
# FFmpegKitNativeVersion is watched, not FFmpegVersion: the two number differently and do not track
# each other (FFmpegKit 8.1.7 packages FFmpeg n8.1.2), and only the FFmpegKit number names an .aar
# that exists upstream. build/native-versions.tsv maps a new one back to its FFmpeg version, which
# is what the package version is based on - so a finding here means "add a row there, then re-pin".
# arthenica/ffmpeg-kit is archived with every release stripped of assets, and ffmpeg-kit-next is
# source-only; dev.ffmpegkit-maintained is the fork that actually publishes .aar files. See the
# README for the full comparison.
# Of the eight variants, ffmpeg-kit-full-gpl is the one checked. They are cut from one build and
# released together, so eight rows would be eight copies of the same finding; if that ever stops
# being true it shows up as the full-gpl download failing to confirm.
# group
FFmpegKit
# Bundled alongside the .aar files by build/.../FetchJars.sh, from its own GitHub releases.
